item.title: First win for Nancy
item.description: Celtic have picked up their first victory under new boss Wilfried Nancy. Two goals in added time meant they got past 10 man Aberdeen 3-1 at Parkhead. Hearts have strengthened their position at the top of the Scottish Premiership with a 2-1 win at home to Rangers. Advertisement The leaders have still lost just once in their 18 league games.

item.title: Multi-agency effort to assist woman after fall on Binn Bán cliff walk
item.description: A multi agency effort took place earlier this afternoon to assist a woman who fell and broke her ankle on the cliff walk at Binn Bán beach. Glenderry Coast Guard unit were surveying the area where a French fishing vessel remains aground when their drones detected the woman in distress. The combined efforts of Glenderry and Dingle Coast guards stretchered the woman to the beach car park, where she was taken by ambulance to Kerry University Hospital. item.title: Tánaiste pays tribute to former Fine Gael TD Gerard Lynch
item.description: The Tánaiste Simon Harris has paid tribute to former Fine Gael TD Gerard Lynch. Mr Lynch passed away yesterday, December 20th, and was a Fine Gael TD for the Kerry North constituency from 1969 to 1977, and a Senator for the Agricultural Panel from 1977 to 1981. He was also a councillor for the Listowel area on Kerry County Council and Listowel Urban District Council during various periods from 1967 to 1979. item.title: Caring for Kerry campaign issues advice to people with chronic illnesses
item.description: This week’s Caring for Kerry message has issued advice for people living with long-term health conditions. People living with long-term or chronic health conditions are more vulnerable to illness in winter. Examples of long-term health conditions include Diabetes, Asthma, COPD and Cardiovascular Disease. Advertisement Those with long-term health conditions are advised to get their annual flu vaccinations, and to stay up to date with other vaccination, as well as taking all prescribed medications

item.title: Liverpool fear Isak has suffered major injury
item.description: Liverpool fear Alexander Isak has suffered a major injury after being forced off in last night's 2-1 win at Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League. The club are waiting for the results of a scan but it's understood there are big concerns over damage to the Sweden international's lower left leg. Isak was hurt scoring the opener, only his second goal since his British record transfer from Newcastle. Advertisement
